title: What If You Stood on the Surface of Pluto?

scenes.text: What if you stood on Pluto? The sky is blue. Nothing else about it is friendly.
The ground is about minus 228 degrees Celsius. Frozen nitrogen, the gas you breathe, covers the surface.
The air is roughly a hundred-thousandth as thick as Earth's. There is nothing there to breathe.
Look up and you'd see about twenty layers of haze, stacked up to 150 kilometers high.
Ahead, mountains of water ice rise around five kilometers tall, standing on ground frozen harder than steel.
And the plain has almost no craters. It's no more than a few hundred million years old. The coldest place you could stand is young.

description:
What if you stood on Pluto?
At about minus 228 degrees Celsius with air a hundred-thousandth as thick as ours, you'd find blue haze, nitrogen ice and mountains of water ice five kilometers tall.
What should we run through next?
